subject.title: Bug: Poe image/video-output models are accepted in config but fail at runtime (Nano Banana 400, Veo/Sora fallback)

question: Should OpenClaw treat custom provider image/video-output model refs as unsupported chat/session models with clear diagnostics, or add a first-class output-modality contract that routes those refs through media generation?
rationale: Both acceptable paths change public provider/model semantics: diagnostics need output-modality metadata or detection, while first-class support requires broader provider, response, tool, and channel contracts.

options.title: Diagnostic-first output contract
options.body: Add or derive output-modality metadata and fail fast when a media-output model is selected for chat/session runtime, while leaving generation on image_generate and video_generate.

options.title: First-class media-output routing
options.body: Add output modality metadata and route image/video-output model refs through media generation runtime with channel delivery support.

options.title: Wait for plugin proof
options.body: Keep core unchanged until a Poe or generic media provider plugin proves the missing API surface and desired workflow.

recommendation.title: Diagnostic-first output contract
recommendation.body: Add or derive output-modality metadata and fail fast when a media-output model is selected for chat/session runtime, while leaving generation on image_generate and video_generate.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans provider catalog semantics, model runtime selection, and media generation routing, where the inspected history points most strongly to steipete.
